story: Meet the Oriental Bay Owl (Phodilus badius), a distinctive bird from the Tytonidae family. Preferring habitats such as Mountain evergreen broadleaf/coniferous forest; secondary forest; mangroves; and lowland moist forest, this species has adapted to thrive under specific environmental conditions. With an IUCN status of Least Concern (LC), its population trends are closely watched by scientists and enthusiasts. The Oriental Bay Owl serves as an indicator species for the health of its environment. Whether you are a seasoned ornithologist or a curious nature lover, learning about the Oriental Bay Owl enriches our understanding of nature.
